scenario: Space plays or pauses; while stopped it starts the track under the cursor, and the card shows Playing or Paused
n / p start the next or previous track in play order, queued tracks first; at either end of the playlist they stop unless repeat all wraps around
h / l seek 10 s, ← / → 5 s, Shift+← / Shift+→ 30 s, 0–9 jump to 0–90 % of the track and Ctrl+J takes a time such as 1:30; the playhead lands there, clamped to the track
+ (or =) and - (or _) step the volume by 5 %, clamped at 0 and 100, and set the macOS system volume; --volume or `volume` in config.toml sets the start level
[ / ] step playback speed by 0.25x between 0.25x and 4x, also while paused; the playhead runs at the new speed and the speed chip shows it
s toggles shuffle (every track once per round) and r cycles repeat off / all / one; the next track follows the indicator, and a manual skip ignores repeat one
z cycles the sleep presets (15, 30, 60 min by default) then off; the status line counts down and playback pauses when it fires, while a track paused before then stays paused with no toast
b marks A, a second b past A marks B and loops A–B, a third b clears the loop; changing track clears it too
j / k or ↓ / ↑ move the cursor, gg / Home and G / End jump to the ends, PageDown / Ctrl+D and PageUp / Ctrl+U page, and Enter plays the selected track
a queues or unqueues the selected track (its row shows its queue number), A queues it next, x takes it out and Shift+↑ / Shift+↓ move it; queued tracks play before the playlist's own next
o cycles the sort order (date added, artist, album, year, favourites first) and f toggles the ★ favourite on the selected track, which survives a restart

d asks to move the selected track to the Trash, naming its title and artist; y or Enter trashes the file and the row leaves once it is in the Trash, n / Esc / q cancel, and a failed trash shows an error toast and keeps the track
S prompts for a name and Enter saves the playlist as an M3U file in the config folder's playlists/, an over-long name cut short; `zefiro --playlist <name>` loads it back in the same order
R rescans the music folder, and files added or removed while zefiro runs show up on their own after a short pause; a folder named like an audio file is not listed
L opens the music-folder prompt prefilled with the current path; Enter saves the trimmed path to config.toml and rescans the new folder

/ opens search: typing narrows the library by title, artist, album or file name, best match first, ↑ / ↓ move, Enter plays, Tab queues, Ctrl+U clears, Ctrl+W deletes a word and Esc closes; in an online server tab it searches the server, albums before tracks
H opens the play history, newest first; j / k and gg / G move, Enter queues the entry's track and Enter again unqueues it, and a track no longer in the library shows the toast `Not in library`
i shows the details (tags, format, path; server and id for a server track) of the selected track, or of the playing one, and any key closes them
? or Ctrl+K opens help listing every action with all its chords joined by ` / `, laid out in as many columns as the terminal fits; Esc, q or Ctrl+K close it

, opens settings and pauses playback while open: j / k move, h / l step, Enter / Space activate, and each change (preset, theme, cover, chips, key hints, animations, layout, crossfade, ReplayGain, output device, sleep presets) applies at once and is saved to config.toml or zefiro-ui.toml with comments kept

a [keymap] entry in config.toml such as `next = "N"` (or a table with a `context`) rebinds that action while zefiro runs and the old chord stops working; a malformed or colliding binding falls back to the default

editing config.toml ([keymap], music_dir), zefiro-ui.toml or the active theme file while zefiro runs applies without a restart; a broken file (e.g. a line `a..b = 1`) keeps the last good values and raises one toast naming the file and the cause

the theme row in settings, `theme` in config.toml or --theme picks one of 16 built-in themes or a themes/<name>.toml file (`auto` = noir), and a switch fades the whole screen to the new colours in 150 ms with Animations on

in kitty, Ghostty, iTerm2 or WezTerm the vinyl or plain cover renders as an image and fades to the next track's art; without terminal graphics those modes draw no cover, milkdrop draws text cells, and off reserves no column
while a track plays, the spectrum row in the card and the milkdrop cover move with the music, and they fade out when it pauses or goes silent

the screen picks the full card, compact or minimal layout from the terminal size, the Layout setting forces compact, hiding key hints gives that row to the playlist, and below 48×16 a too-small notice shows
with crossfade at 0 s consecutive tracks play gapless; at 0.5–10 s (settings or `audio.crossfade`) a track that ends on its own fades into the next, while a skip cuts

the Output device setting cycles the system default and each named device; a switch shows `Playing on <device>` once, a device that disappears falls back to the system default with a toast, and losing output while playing pauses with `Output lost — paused`
on macOS, Now Playing in the menu bar / Control Center shows the track, its artwork and an elapsed time that runs at the playback speed, and pauses with zefiro

u adds a Subsonic/Navidrome server in three steps (http(s) link, user, password shown as dots); the server is saved in config.toml, its password in the macOS keychain once the server accepts it, and it reconnects on the next start
c lists the servers with their state; j / k select, Enter edits one, t reconnects it, d asks to remove it (Enter removes, Esc goes back) and u adds another

Tab / Shift+Tab switch between the local library and each server's tab, Enter opens an album (Backspace goes back) and Enter on a track streams it with the album as the playlist, starting once the first 512 KB arrive; an offline server shows a toast instead
server tracks download in 4 MB chunks into ~/Library/Caches/zefiro/media, a cached track replays with no request, and the cache stays under 2 GB by evicting the oldest files first
server tracks played past half their length (at most 4 min) are scrobbled to their server, and scrobbles made while it is offline are kept on disk and sent once it is back, also after a restart
q quits: playback stops, pending settings and unsent scrobbles are written, and the terminal and window colours are restored
u opens the server form laid out like a huh form (a field per line with its hint and error under it), and every text prompt shows a block cursor
every text prompt ends in a block cursor of one reversed cell, also on an empty field's placeholder
/ in a server view filters it in place (locally for Playlists and opened lists, through search3 for Songs and Albums); Enter keeps the filter and Esc clears it
the local tab always lists the scanned library and is titled Library while a server track plays; Enter there plays the library, and n / p walk the list the play started from
the local tab is titled Library while a server track plays
v inside an opened server album or playlist closes it and moves to the next view; the key hints name Tab (Sources), v, o and Backspace
the key hints name the keys of the tab
the music folder prompt lists subfolders, marks those with audio, filters them as you type and completes the selected one with Tab
the music folder prompt draws the subfolders and marks those with audio
the Keychain never shows a system dialog: interaction is off and a denied read reads as a missing password
`zefiro --help` describes every option and `--version` answers with the name and package version
`zefiro --version` prints the name and the package version
a server track's cover art comes through getCoverArt, asked once by its id and then answered from the file
a server track asks for its cover once, the next track of the album asks nothing, and a failed fetch leaves the empty cover with no toast
a player report from before a seek is dropped by revision and leaves the playhead at the target
every wait shows the Dot spinner, stepping ten times a second and asking frames only while shown

a, play-next, dequeue and move act on a server row like on a local one; local and server tracks share one queue in order; a queued server track streams on Ended or n; forgetting a server drops its queued tracks
a queued server row shows its queue number and server tabs show the a Queue hint
